discovery: Discovery of gamma-ray burst afterglows, establishing the cosmological origin of gamma-ray bursts

nominees.name: Enrico Costa
nominees.affiliation: INAF - Istituto di Astrofisica e Planetologia Spaziali, Rome, Italy

motivation: For thirty years gamma-ray bursts were the most energetic phenomena known, yet their distance was unknown to within a factor of a billion. In 1997 Costa and Frontera, using the BeppoSAX Wide Field Cameras and rapid follow-up, discovered the fading X-ray afterglow of GRB 970228, providing arcminute positions for the first time. That made optical and radio counterparts possible. Kulkarni and collaborators measured the redshift of GRB 970508 and detected its radio afterglow, whose scintillation showed relativistic expansion. Together these results showed that bursts are cosmological explosions releasing about 10^51-10^52 erg in collimated relativistic jets, linked to the collapse of massive stars and to compact-object mergers. They turned a qualitative mystery into quantitative physics of energetics, beaming and shocks. They also created the multiwavelength time-domain astronomy that led to the kilonova counterpart of GW170817.
